body:
Ares is providing a unitranche at around 6x leverage for the acquisition of Swedish vehicle glass repair company Cary Group by a consortium comprising existing shareholder Nordic Capital as well as Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan and CPP Investments, according to 9fin sources.

Jefferies advised on the sale, marketing Cary Group off €187m of structuring EBITDA, the sources said. At 6x, that would imply a unitranche of around €1.1bn.

CVC announced on 17 November that it would sell its stake of roughly 50% to the consortium, with the deal expected to close in H1 27.

Banks had pitched debt packages at up to 5.5x leverage for the buyout, 9fin previously reported.

Cary Group repairs and replaces vehicle glass and offers auto body repair. It operates around 1,800 workshops across 13 countries.

Nordic Capital bought a majority stake in the business in 2018 and took it private alongside CVC in 2022.

Ares, CPP Investments, CVC, Jefferies and Nordic Capital declined to comment. Cary Group and Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan did not respond to requests for comment.
